title: Adaptive Model Scheduling for Resource-efficient Data Labeling
motivation: Multiple resource-hungry models needed for comprehensive labeling, but executing all models on all data is infeasible due to limited computing resources and stringent delay constraints.
problem_framing: Submodular function maximization with knapsack constraints where model output values are unknown until execution, making classic optimization approaches infeasible.
key_insight: Executed models' outputs provide semantic hints about unexecuted models' outputs; a DRL agent can learn these implicit relationships to predict model value before execution.
method_signature: DRL-based model value prediction combined with cost-profit greedy scheduling under deadline or deadline-memory constraints.
evaluation_criteria: Execution time savings (53% with full recall) and value recall rate improvement (132%-310% vs random scheduling under 0.5s deadline).
negative_result_or_admitted_limitation: Knowledge transfer degrades when content distributions diverge (e.g., training on dog images, testing on human actions); requires 10%-20% of dataset for adequate training samples.
evidence_for_taste: handcrafted rules are cumbersome and inefficient when there are tens of models
classic submodular optimization approaches infeasible to solve our problem
cost-Q greedy algorithm performs better than provable guarantee 1-1/e
knowledge learned from the other dataset with different content distribution can also optimize scheduling effectively
a large portion of computing resources could be wasted without careful model selection
thinking_moves: Prove evaluation function is submodular to characterize problem structure, then pivot to DRL because classic approaches cannot handle unknown values
Model outputs become observations that inform predictions about unexecuted models - frame as sequential decision problem
Separate prediction component (DRL) from scheduling algorithms to enable flexible deployment under different resource constraints
Admit handcrafted rules fail at scale, requiring data-driven approach to discover model relationships automatically
